clue.text: Whom a solecism might stir up badly ?

definitions.text: Whom a solecism might stir up badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the two words stir up are to be jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about the sort of person who is upset by a grammatical blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the letters of STIR UP; the whole clue also describes the answer, a stickler whom a solecism annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant who insists on correct usage is exactly the person a grammatical error would annoy.

clue.text: Violinist and heathen in one

parts.note: a heathen is a pagan
taken as written
the Roman numeral one is I

explanation.surface: Someone who is both a fiddler and a non-believer.
explanation.walkthrough: Niccolò Paganini was the famous Italian violin virtuoso.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was an Italian virtuoso fiddle player and composer.

clue.text: Make second stage appearance

parts.note: an actor coming back on to the stage in a play for a second time

explanation.surface: An actor coming back for another scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who comes back on stage after an exit goes in again.

clue.text: Rodents climbing on the table? Right

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rats are rodents
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Rats scrambling up on to the dining table, quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses RATS to STAR in this down clue; 'on' puts it above BOARD. Right is the right-hand side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The right side of a ship, facing forward, is called starboard.

clue.text: Keeping, a store of hosiery.

definitions.meaning: keeping a store of goods is holding them in stock
a leg garment, one item of hosiery

explanation.surface: Someone running a shop that sells socks and tights.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep supplies is to stock them; and a long knitted leg covering is an item of hosiery.

clue.text: The sweet, enchanting Sultana ?

definitions.meaning: a gel confection dusted with sugar
a sultan's wife who delights a Turkish ruler

explanation.surface: Praise for a beautiful sultan's wife, or for a dried grape.
explanation.walkthrough: Sultana looks like the dried grape, a sweet thing; it is the wife of a sultan, a Turk's delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose-flavoured jelly sweet carries this name, and a charming sultan's consort would delight a Turk.

clue.text: Murphy's pile ?

parts.note: murphy is slang for a potato, and the pile is a heap of them stored under straw and earth

explanation.surface: A heap belonging to a man named Murphy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murphy' is old slang for a potato; this word is a heap of potatoes covered with straw and earth for winter storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers store potatoes in a mound covered with earth and straw, which is known by this name.

clue.text: Entreat the little devil to look about

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
lo is an old word for look
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Begging the imp to glance around.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or plead with someone is to entreat them.

clue.text: Henry's' last wife, having once been to sea.?

definitions.text: Henry's' last wife, having once been to sea

parts.words: Henry's' last wife, having once been to sea
parts.note: Henry VIII's last wife was Catherine Parr, and a parr is a young salmon; one that has been to sea once and returned

explanation.surface: Catherine Parr, sixth wife of Henry VIII, after a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII's last wife was Catherine PARR; a parr is a young salmon, and once it has made one trip to sea and come back it takes this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A young salmon returning to fresh water after its first year at sea is so named.

clue.text: Synge's holiday trippers?

parts.note: J. M. Synge's one-act play title read as people travelling to the seaside

explanation.surface: Tourists in the writings of the Irish dramatist Synge.
explanation.walkthrough: J. M. Synge's one-act tragedy set on the Aran Islands has this title; read literally, it describes people going to the coast on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Synge's play about Aran Islanders also describes travellers heading for the coast.

clue.text: The old shell-thrower is incomparably heroic

definitions.meaning: a soldier who once hurled hand bombs (grenades)
the song The British ... says none of the world's great heroes can compare with this soldier

explanation.surface: Praise for a brave old soldier who lobbed shells.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on the British marching song 'The British Grenadiers', whose words claim no hero can compare with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Such soldiers were first picked to throw grenades, and the regimental song hails them as beyond compare among heroes.

clue.text: Support makes us turn one up after a quiet start

indicators.note: after places the turned phrase behind the opening a quiet letters

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the phrase one up backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that support requires turning one up after a slow, quiet start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses I + UP to give PUI, which goes after A and P (quiet). An appui is a support or prop, a term borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Appui is a French-derived word for a prop or point of support, used in fencing and military terms.

clue.text: Remarkable lack of furniture

definitions.meaning: read as ..., an absence of one piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Commenting that a room's emptiness is striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking is worth noting; and split as 'no table' it describes a missing item of furniture.

clue.text: It's wicked! Just one member 'promises to pay

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I
MP, Member of Parliament
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: An outraged cry that a single politician is just signing debts away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' is a link word; the definition 'It's wicked' needs reading as 'it is wicked', an adjective sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverence toward God was counted wickedness, so ungodly behaviour is called wicked.

clue.text: She's not a graduate either

parts.note: nor means and not, here completed by the clue's closing either
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that a woman, like another, never finished university.
explanation.walkthrough: NORMA is the title heroine of Bellini's opera, so a woman's name serves for 'She'. 'not ... either' is the sense of NOR, and 'either' closes that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's name, famously the druid priestess heroine of Bellini's opera, so 'she' stands for her.

clue.text: Glass vessel

definitions.meaning: a tall beer or sherry glass
a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large drinking glass for sherry or beer and a two-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: Trouble a mile from the old rallying-point

indicators.note: trouble as a verb means stir up or disturb, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Some unrest a mile away from an old meeting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' is an instruction to stir up the letters of A MILE FROM. The oriflamme was the sacred red banner of France, a standard to rally round.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred banner of the abbey of St Denis served medieval French kings as a standard to gather behind in battle.

clue.text: Take-off for one' sort of plane

definitions.meaning: an aircraft lifting straight up, as with a jump jet
a plane in geometry standing upright

explanation.surface: An aircraft taking off, and a type of aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' looks like an aircraft but means a flat surface in geometry; 'Take-off' is one example of upright motion, as in VTOL jets.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright describes both a jump jet's straight-up take-off and a flat surface standing at right angles to the horizontal.

clue.text: Front-line M.O. honoured by Cabinet ?

parts.note: the front line is where war is fought
a medical officer is a doctor, DR
OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour given to someone

explanation.surface: A frontline army doctor being decorated by the government ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Cabinet the body of ministers handing out an honour; it is a piece of furniture for clothes. OBE is a British honour, an Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cupboard for hanging clothes is a kind of cabinet.

clue.text: Increase. Aunt Meg's confusion

indicators.note: confusion means the letters of the aunt's name are muddled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An aunt getting more and more muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' scrambles AUNT MEG; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment something is to make it greater, that is, to add to it.

clue.text: Senseless to involve the girl with'the gun

indicators.note: involve in its old sense of entangle or twist up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: Annie Oakley, the sharpshooter of the musical Annie Get Your Gun

explanation.surface: A remark that it is pointless to drag a gunwoman into things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the girl with the gun' is ANNIE, from the musical 'Annie Get Your Gun'; 'to involve' tangles her letters into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something silly and pointless lacks sense.

clue.text: Austere old Bob has a vinegary exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the vinegary word goes round the outside of the shilling letter

parts.note: acetic means relating to vinegar
a bob was slang for the old British shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: A stern old man called Bob with a sour outer manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name but is slang for a shilling, the old British coin before 1971, written s. 'has a vinegary exterior' puts ACETIC around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person practising strict self-denial lives a severe, austere life.

clue.text: Harsh sounding yarn

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for harsh is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: harsh can mean cruel

explanation.surface: A harsh-sounding story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a tale; it is a fine worsted wool for embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: A loosely twisted worsted wool used in embroidery is a kind of yarn.

clue.text: Jumbo alone is so mischievous

definitions.meaning: an elephant living apart from its herd is called a rogue, so it is rogue-like

explanation.surface: A lone elephant described as naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: A rogue elephant is one that lives alone, away from the herd, and is often dangerous; 'Jumbo' is a classic name for an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful naughtiness is like a rogue's, and a lone elephant is a rogue.

clue.text: Would central heating impair this residence?

definitions.text: Would central heating impair this residence

parts.words: Would central heating impair this residence
parts.note: a home made of snow blocks would melt if heated

explanation.surface: Asking whether installing radiators would damage a house.
explanation.walkthrough: An ice house would melt if heated.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome built from blocks of snow would melt with too much warmth.

clue.text: Forbidden to be unwell in charge of it

parts.note: unwell means ill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being sick while in charge of something is not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful or banned is forbidden.

clue.text: A revolutionary invention

parts.note: revolutionary in the sense of turning round, not of changing the world

explanation.surface: Praise for a world-changing discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests something that transforms society; here it means something that rotates.
explanation.definitionFit: A round thing that spins on an axle is literally revolving, and it was a famous early invention.

clue.text: Diagrammatic reconstruction of Tim's cache

indicators.note: reconstruction means the letters of the following words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A diagram showing how Tim's hidden store was rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstruction' rearranges the letters of TIM'S CACHE, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing that shows the layout of parts in outline is schematic, that is, in the form of a diagram.

clue.text: According to the text we hear it's the coastal strip

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for according to the text is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: literal means following the exact words of the text

explanation.surface: A reader explaining what a written passage says about the shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' shows that LITERAL (according to the text) sounds like the word for a shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: The littoral is the zone along the shore of a sea or lake, a strip of land by the coast.

clue.text: Its lead decreases and it often draws

definitions.text: Its lead decreases and it often draws

parts.words: Its lead decreases and it often draws
parts.note: the lead is its graphite core worn down by use, and draws means sketches, not ties in a game

explanation.surface: A sports team whose lead keeps shrinking and which often ties its matches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a team losing its lead and drawing games; 'lead' is the graphite core and 'draws' means sketches.
explanation.definitionFit: A writing tool whose graphite core wears down with use is commonly used for sketching.
